lines.caption: This is a tour of the pull request for issue 143: while you rename a file in place, Tab saves it and renames the next file.
lines.say: This is a tour of the pull request for issue one forty-three: while you rename a file in place, Tab saves it and renames the next file.

lines.caption: It has three parts: what this PR adds, how it was built and verified, and what comes later.
Part 1. What this PR adds.
The name entry's key handler now handles Tab and Shift+Tab, and a new test drives them.
lines.say: The name entry's key handler now handles Tab and Shift Tab, and a new test drives them.

lines.caption: You press Tab in the F2 name entry, in the Details view. Shift+Tab goes back instead.
lines.say: You press Tab in the F two name entry, in the Details view. Shift Tab goes back instead.

lines.caption: First the name is checked. An invalid one shows the error and the entry stays, with nothing saved.
Then the next or previous row is picked, in the order you see it, before saving, skipping launchers.
The name is saved through the usual F2 path. A name you didn't change saves nothing.
lines.say: The name is saved through the usual F two path. A name you didn't change saves nothing.

lines.caption: The next entry opens, with the row selected and the name selected without its extension.
You type and press Tab again. On the last row, Tab just saves and stops; there's no wrap-around.
Before this, renaming a run of files meant F2 on each one. Nemo and Dolphin let Tab jump to the next name.
lines.say: Before this, renaming a run of files meant F two on each one. Nemo and Dolphin let Tab jump to the next name.

lines.caption: The next file is picked before saving, because the renamed file may sort to a different row.
Step 1: the handler catches Tab and keypad Tab. With Ctrl or Alt held, Tab is left to GTK as before.
lines.say: Step one: the handler catches Tab and keypad Tab. With Control or Alt held, Tab is left to G T K as before.

lines.caption: Step 2: the text is checked the way Up and Down already check it. An invalid name keeps the entry open.
lines.say: Step two: the text is checked the way Up and Down already check it. An invalid name keeps the entry open.

lines.caption: Step 3: a new function walks the rows into expanded folders and back out, and skips desktop launchers.
lines.say: Step three: a new function walks the rows into expanded folders and back out, and skips desktop launchers.

lines.caption: Step 4: editing ends exactly as Return ends it, and the key is kept from moving the focus.
lines.say: Step four: editing ends exactly as Return ends it, and the key is kept from moving the focus.

lines.caption: Step 5: the next edit is queued through the same idle step that F2 uses.
lines.say: Step five: the next edit is queued through the same idle step that F two uses.

lines.caption: Step 6: you type the next name, then Tab, Return or Escape. The first and last rows stop instead of wrapping.
lines.say: Step six: you type the next name, then Tab, Return or Escape. The first and last rows stop instead of wrapping.

lines.caption: Tab moves down, Shift+Tab moves up, and at either end the name is saved and the entry closes.
lines.say: Tab moves down, Shift Tab moves up, and at either end the name is saved and the entry closes.

lines.caption: An invalid name stays put, an unchanged name moves on, and a launcher row is skipped.
Ctrl+Tab and Alt+Tab are unchanged, and so are the icon and compact views, which keep the popover.
lines.say: Control Tab and Alt Tab are unchanged, and so are the icon and compact views, which keep the popover.

lines.caption: Here is the new branch: check, pick the neighbour, end the edit, then open the next one.
The PR changes one source file, adds a test, and adds this page and its narration.
To undo it, revert the PR. It stores nothing, so there is nothing else to clean up.
Part 2. How it was built and verified.
It was built and tested on the first commit. The review fixes after it were only syntax-checked, and CI runs them.
lines.say: It was built and tested on the first commit. The review fixes after it were only syntax checked, and C I runs them.

lines.caption: It builds on the in-place rename from issue 16, and its test, whose setup the new test copies.
lines.say: It builds on the in-place rename from issue sixteen, and its test, whose setup the new test copies.

lines.caption: The debs built with no warnings in changed files, and all 32 tests passed in the cloud container.
lines.say: The debs built with no warnings in changed files, and all thirty-two tests passed in the cloud container.

lines.caption: The new test passed in 24 seconds, and the issue 16 rename test still passed.
lines.say: The new test passed in twenty-four seconds, and the issue sixteen rename test still passed.

lines.caption: The review fixes were only syntax-checked, not rebuilt or re-run here.
lines.say: The review fixes were only syntax checked, not rebuilt or re-run here.

lines.caption: Not run: a failing rename while the next entry is open, and row order with expanded folders.
The local code review, at high, reported 4 findings and fixed 3 of them.
lines.say: The local code review, at high, reported four findings and fixed three of them.

lines.caption: Tab now skips launchers, leaves Ctrl and Alt Tab to GTK, and the test proves a fixed name still saves.
lines.say: Tab now skips launchers, leaves Control and Alt Tab to G T K, and the test proves a fixed name still saves.

lines.caption: It skipped the missing explainer, which this page resolves, and a check that a shot already shows.
CI reviews the first push at high too, and posts its findings in the code review comment.
lines.say: C I reviews the first push at high too, and posts its findings in the code review comment.

lines.caption: CI builds the review fixes and re-runs every test on the first push.
lines.say: C I builds the review fixes and re-runs every test on the first push.

lines.caption: A failing rename and expanded folders first get tried when you use it.
To see it yourself, open the issue, the changes, and the test with its shots in CI's verify comment.
Part 3. What comes later.
Nothing depends on this issue yet. Issue 144 comes next in the batch only because it edits the same file.
lines.say: Nothing depends on this issue yet. Issue one forty-four comes next in the batch only because it edits the same file.

lines.caption: So 144 waits for this PR, and finds its functions by name, since this PR moved its line numbers.
lines.say: So one forty-four waits for this PR, and finds its functions by name, since this PR moved its line numbers.

lines.caption: In short: Tab and Shift+Tab let you rename a run of files without pressing F2 for each one.
lines.say: In short: Tab and Shift Tab let you rename a run of files without pressing F two for each one.
